newsitem.title: UK: Support crumbles, London gold drifts lower.
newsitem.headline: Support crumbles, London gold drifts lower.

text.p: Gold edged below $385 support in very thin conditions on Monday afternoon and many players expected to see further selling hit the market.
"A break below $385 should sent it down to $382," one said.
Gold fixed at $384.60 per ounce compared to $385.00 in the morning and a Friday London close of $385.20/$385.80.
Prices were teetering on the brink all morning and just before the fix the $385 level gave way.
By 1412 GMT, the spot price had gone as low as $383.30 against its intra-day high of $385.30. Prices have been sliding since August 26 and 27, when they touched highs around $390.
Most recently, the market has been disappointed that U.S. missile attacks on Iraq last week and strong U.S. jobs data on Friday failed to perk up the market.
Ahead of the fix, the market had been divided on the near-term direction and many were awaiting a convincing break one way or the other before committing themselves.
"I'd feel much more comfortable selling at $384.50 than at $385," one dealer had said.
Below the $382 support level, prices would approach the key $380 area, the lowest prices seen since the market slid from February highs around $418.
The market would be watching the Comex options expiry on Friday, dealers added.
Silver also slid, falling as low as $5.05 per ounce support before bouncing slightly. At 1435 GMT, it had recovered to $5.08/$5.10 per ounce, a loss of six cents on Friday's London close.
The range for silver quotes so far on Monday had been $5.05 to $5.13.
Below $5.05, dealers and analysts expect support to kick in at the psychological $5.00 level, then at July lows of $4.93.
Platinum was only slightly easier around $394 per ounce.
Support for platinum was pegged at $393, then at $390.
Palladium was little changed, with bids quoted so far from $125.85 down to $123.50.
